item.title: Intertemporal Boots (Revisted): Intertemporal Boots (Revisted)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes.

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout (Optional): [How will you structure the page in terms of information presentation, or plot development? If you plan on using a unique format/format screw, describe that here.]

Elevator Pitch: The SCP is a pair of boots that allows the user to walk through time as well as space. We can all walk through space and we understand how our bodies interact with space as we move, the SCP allows it's user to walk through time as well as space.

Central Narrative: The foundation finds the boots in a raid against a Marshall, Carter, and Dark auction. They contain it without issue and label the anomaly "Safe." As the foundation tests the boots, they find that moving on the x and z-axis causes the wearer to blink around the timeline in strange ways (D-Class appearing at other Foundation sites in the past, D-Class appearing in other SCP tests in the future, etc.) The D-Class is always returned via a temporal anchor.

A previous raid on an MC&D facility revealed how MC&D planned to use the SCP to further their own underground network of selling anomalous goods. The boots were going to send a user to the future of a planned auction location to see if the auction would be raided or not. MC&D was unable to complete this due to a collection of Foundation raids. The Foundation doesn't have any records of any MC&D raids on the listed days.

+ the good stuff
- here it is

Some text to show/hide.


In a classified part of the document, the higher staff of the foundation will learn that the boots are a Thaumiel class and have been occasionally used to alter past events to the foundation's favor. Those strange unlisted Foundation raids were the current day Foundation using the boots to leap into the past to guarantee that MC&D don't use the boots. Agents would go back in time and sabotage MC&D's testing by raiding the tests.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: This article creates a time paradox/self-fulfilling prophecy around a somewhat easy to understand anomaly. Reminds me of the Series I/II style of anomaly.

Additional Notes: I'm going to need a couple of other heads to weigh in on this, especially the punchline of the article. Time paradoxes are really fun to write, but they can be messy, so I need some senior staff to help me iron out the kinks.

item.title: Jeanne's Home for Strange and Lost Creatures: Jeanne's Home for Strange and Lost Creatures
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout (Optional):
- House description

- Experiments with the house

- Jeanne description, interview

- Event: New family member arrives

- Jeanne post-event interview

- Notes on the house's other residents

Elevator Pitch: At its core, Jeanne's Home for Strange and Lost Creatures is intended to be proof that the anomalous isn't always sinister or scary. The Home is a group of varying anomalous individuals who live together in a "bigger-on-the-inside," sentient house. The Foundation has secured the property but has established that the Home poses a minimal threat.

Central Narrative: The overall story of Jeanne's Home for Strange and Lost Creatures is that is a tight-knit community of anomalous individuals that does not much appreciate outsiders, namely the Foundation, encroaching on it. This is characterized by the initial hostility that the Wooden Marionette expresses, That Other Guy's continued refusal to reveal himself to Foundation Scientists, and the foreboding noises coming from the Dream Garden. The house, and its residents, put up with the Foundation's presence because they don't want to give up what they have. It is loosely implied, but not confirmed, that Dr. John Hammond (The lead Foundation scientist at the Home) is developing feelings for Jeanne, the owner of the home.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The concept of a benevolent anomaly that attracts and gathers others around it is something I haven't seen before. Each resident is unique, and the main purpose of that was to humanize each of the anomalies and prove that sometimes SCPs can be people, too. Jeanne's Home for Strange and Lost Creatures is a prime example of humanity's ability to develop bonds even in the coldest and most sterile circumstances.

Additional Notes: The Home was originally created as a fan-piece for the Unfounded canon, as a place where some of the more overtly anomalous beings could live in safety. The title "Jeanne's Home for Strange and Lost Creatures" is a nod to a children's book, written by Ben Hatke, of a similar name.

item.title: Gnome tree (repost): Gnome tree (repost)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Festive/ Horror

Page Layout (Optional):

Elevator Pitch: The Gnome Tree Is a Classic Christmas tree, but with a twist, Sometimes, there are Animate Small, limbless Scandinavian Christmas Gnomes, such as dolls and ornaments, while outside of the tree, these gnomes are quite mischievous, sometimes when the tree ejects non anomalous Christmas Decorations, and these gnomes will attempt to ‘Decorate’ the containment cell, along with covering up CCTV footage

Central Narrative: These Gnomes Have a Rigid Hierarchy, where each different Gnome does it’s designed task, The Lowest in the hierarchy, The Gnome Guards, can do very simple tasks, as long as there is a group of three or more or them, these Guards are so Basic, that they have been known to accept orders from almost any life form, including humans, making it possible for testing with the object

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The tree is actually a portal to a Subterranean Festively decorated village. Where countless numbers of these gnomes reside, on a Exploration into the village with a D-Class, the live body cam footage shown gnomes never seen before, like the leader of this village, when the D-Class if found, hundreds of Gnomes Gather around him, and then made Syncretized attack, body footage cuts off for only a few disturbing images to be shown, after the footage comes back on, it shows two guard gnomes studying what the camera is, body footage cuts off again only to show A Tied up D-Class carried on his back into a large Factory located on the right side of the village, where gnomes were shown to put materials such as wool and cotton though the one side, and a dozen gnomes come out of the other side, after the D-Class was fully inside of the Factory, on the other side An Entire Army of Lower Hierarchy Gnomes, along with some High Hierarchy Gnomes

item.title: SCP Idea: Pinular Gas: SCP Idea: Pinular Gas
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout (Optional): I don't really know how I would put this, so if you want to see the sandbox page just ask.

Elevator Pitch:
There's a gas that when inhaled causes negative affects on the victim.
*This gas slowly turns the victims into Wood.
*If the wood corpse of the victim has a piece remove, the piece removed will melt into a pile of skin-like material and blood that is classified as SCP-XXXX-2
*If the victim is taken to the desired area they have after inhalation, they will be free of the negative affects and mutate into SCP-XXXX-3.

Central Narrative: None at the moment, may have a new instance in the future.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The reason for this to stick out or to make it popular is for the following reasons:

  • It may be the first SCP to be a gas that upon inhalation begins a transformation process
  • After inhalation, the situation becomes life or death, as the subject must be transported to their desired location to survive.

Additional Notes: The last time I had posted, it ended up reaching -14 ratings, and that made me very disappointed in myself, so my goal is to make my SCP more likable.
Another goal of mine is to get some help with any grammar mess-ups on my article, as well as making the article's input more eloquent.

item.title: Super Mario Syndicate: Super Mario Syndicate
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Media/Satire/Surrealism

Elevator Pitch: A ROM hack of Super Mario World in which every Mario and Luigi who ever died form a union, the levels are the offices of major videogame companies and the sites of riots where police brutality occurred.

Central Narrative: Millions of Marios and Luigis live in a union building, where they raise all the Baby Marios lost in Yoshi's Island. Play of the game has been tied to various spinal compression industries in videogame executives which led to the discovery and tracking of the anomalous ROM. In the wake of various Riots, new "Lost Levels" are encountered where the player can jump on the heads of police officers. This leads to the liquidation of an entire police precinct in an undisclosed US city. The Foundation has trained speed-runners in the Media Department who can play through as pacifists to safely explore. A sub-faction, Luigi's For Ethical Treatment of Yoshi's (LFETY), is discovered, and horribly executes Mario's with dual-Yoshi-bisection (similar to horse quartering) who have performed the Yoshi Sacrifice to complete Star Road. The bisected Mario's are still alive, those who have used a Fire Flower can burn themselves to death.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Everyone's favorite videogame meets political violence.

Additional Notes: Early draft is done, could use more fleshing out but I like the idea of a fairly concise Media SCP that evokes a concept without having to do elaborated logs and progression/reclassification narrative. Someone made a Communist Mario 3 ROM with a great image to headline with attribution.

item.title: Kendall Jenner Pepsi Ad: Kendall Jenner Pepsi Ad
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Media/Satire/Infiltration

Elevator Pitch: An anomalous version of the infamous Kendall Jenner Pepsi ad that iterates until it begins depicting the Foundation as the police and begins detailing containment procedures.

Central Narrative: DOGM OVIE format, we iterate through increasingly lurid, then occult iterations of the Pepsi ad, the artist, journalist, nature of the protest and police counter-measures, as well as the behavior of the Pepsi drinking officer, all change progressive until things becoming chillingly specific. All testing is ceased, an analyst from the Media Department who has watched the video 5000 times is put through a Loyalty Test, deemed non-compromised, left under surveillance. Some time later the SCP is reclassified to Euclid from Safe when a secondary -A effect is discovered where each playback has cast a sort of radiation, which has collided with several other SCPs and empowered them.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The thematically most vile, yet nihilistic, piece of media ever produced as a virulent media SCP, possible Chaos Insurgency attempt at infiltration.

Additional Notes: Already drafted, mostly formatted (need help with the wiki-table format), ~2.4k words. Playback descriptions follow format of:

item.title: SCP IDEA: "Home": Re: SCP IDEA: "Home"
item.content:encoded:
Resummoned via PM:

Hi again Agent Frog. Thanks for clarifying your central narrative. What you've given us is a good exploration log (the MTF raiding the place and never returning). The problem is how do we get to this point (how was the village discovered initially by the Foundation), and what happens after (the Foundation will not allow a missing MTF team to go unanswered).

More importantly, you haven't provided us with an explanation to the village's existence. Why does it create such anomalous effects? Is there a reason you've tied the main emotion to nostalgia?

item.title: Freddy's Fishman (seeking Greenlight & Critique): Re: Freddy's Fishman (seeking Greenlight & Critique)
item.content:encoded:
Summoned via PM:

Hi there Dr Elliot Anemone. Apologies for the delay in getting this critique to you. Let’s take a look at your concept.

+ crit
- crit

While the idea sounds interesting, and the new, proposed GoI has potential, I feel your Central Narrative has a couple of convenient conjectures that don’t really hold up to scrutiny. I’ll list a couple below for you to iron out:

after something interfered with the communications between the foundation and the agents

What interfered with the communications? Is this crucial to the story, or simply a way for you (the author) to get the MTF captured? Speaking of being captured, what happens to the MTF? You quickly go into another set of Foundation agents who discover the scp – why not simply start your discovery log at this point? Was there a need for the MTF to go in first?

Doctor Josef Monstrosity thanking the foundation for finding their med students projects, and left this one as a show of thanks.

Why would this gesture be “a show of thanks”?

attempts by the Foundation to gain the Fishmans trust in hopes that it is capable of telling the Foundation where it came from

If it were experimented on by the medical students, wouldn’t the Fishman automatically side with the Foundation? Why the resistance to give up a place and people who tortured it?

Dr. Franklin, a young researcher with vague origins, but was brought in by the higher ups so staff just decide it's best not to question it

Again, this sounds dubious at best, unprofessional at worst. You’ve introduced a character to advance the story, and nothing else. There’s no reason for his inclusion at this point unless you have a good explanation for his appearance.

how it went to the hospital willingly at first because when it was human it had aquagenic urticaria and the hospital said they could cure him

This is a good motivation for the scip to have, and an excellent introduction to what the new GoI is capable / not capable of doing. The problem is you seem to have given us conflicting views of what the GoI actually is: is it a place for so-called monsters to go to get cured or experimented on?

how the Hospital views normalcy as an illness that needs to be remedied.

This, then, becomes even more problematic as you have an additional goal for the GoI. Why was it experimenting on the fish-man then? Wouldn’t it view all mutants as normal people?

Lots of plot inconsistencies I hope you can help clear up. If you decide to revise the concept / respond below, do drop me another PM and I’ll do my best to take another look. For now, all the best!

item.title: "The Brain Game" a rough pitch: Re: "The Brain Game" a rough pitch
item.content:encoded:
On further consideration, you should consider how on-site soldiers are pawns, researchers are rooks, some perhaps humanoid Thaumiels on site are like Knights, some powerful tech or Thaumiel objects are rooks, the site director is the king and the lead researcher on this SCP is the Queen. Characterize some of these. Then on the SCP's side, it's the King, a Keter it makes a deal with to engineer a breach is the queen, lesser SCPs are the rest, and it's a chess game.

Or, mechanisms around site locks/sub-systems that the SCP compromises. Perhaps a mix.

Another key criticism you'll face is, how is this not just a non-anomalous AI. 079 seems more anomalous because it's an advanced AI from the 70s, and it was early series. You'll need to emphasize the preternatural jump in capability of the, presumably very basic Chess-expert algo, which shouldn't have any means to bootstrap general intelligence.

item.title: First SCP.: Re: First SCP.
item.content:encoded:
Summoned via PM:

Hi there Melvin Dukowski. Apologies for the delay in getting this critique to you. Let’s take a look at your concept.

So I like this a lot: it’s simple, straightforward, and you have potential for some body horror here (whether human or beast). I also appreciate that you’ve done your research on Sarkic lore, and feel you’ve got the basics down.

My only question right now is how you plan on presenting the article. It seems like you’ve got your central narrative in order, but how will you plan on telling the story? If you could give us a brief breakdown of your page components, that will help us visualise the article better. Will you have discovery or testing logs, for example? If so, what happens (briefly) in them?

If you decide to revise the concept / respond below, do drop me another PM and I’ll do my best to take another look. For now, all the best!

item.title: "The Brain Game" a rough pitch: Re: "The Brain Game" a rough pitch
item.content:encoded:
I like AI SCPs, AI is the big fear on the horizon, totally uncanny and unpredictable. I think it escaping into a robot body is retro and a bit campy, so if you want to go in that direction, make sure you nail those notes.

If you want to go in a slightly meta-direction, have the SCP essentially use its chess strategy against the Foundation characters trying to isolate and contain its outbreak. I'd recommend something like a site breach instead of an outdoors situation. You can end with some kind of checkmate and make it cliff-hanger-y. Just some quick sauce from my perusal, I'd greenlight the draft if I had the power.
